articles.title: BSTU Ranked 858th in Global GreenMetric University Rankings
articles.excerpt: Bukhara State Technical University has been ranked 858th in the global ranking of universities committed to achieving the Green Sustainability Index by the UI GreenMetric World University Rankings.
paragraphs: Bukhara State Technical University (BSTU) has officially been ranked 858th in the global ranking of universities committed to achieving a Green Sustainability Index, as determined by the internationally recognized UI GreenMetric World University Rankings.

The GreenMetric ranking is an independent global initiative that evaluates universities on six key sustainability criteria: Setting & Infrastructure, Energy & Climate Change, Waste Management, Water Conservation, Transportation, and Education & Research. BSTU's inclusion in this prestigious global ranking reflects the university's dedicated commitment to environmental stewardship and sustainable development.

BSTU's ranking is a direct result of sustained investments in campus greening programs, including extensive tree-planting campaigns across university grounds, clean energy installations, smart water irrigation systems in the botanical gardens, and active participation in national environmental programs such as the 'Green Space' project initiated by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.

The university administration has set ambitious targets to improve BSTU's global ranking by expanding renewable energy usage, establishing a campus waste sorting and composting system, and launching dedicated environmental science research projects in partnership with international universities.
articles.author: BSTU Communications Office

articles.title: Cabinet Resolution No. 75: Science-Business Cooperation for Sustainability
articles.excerpt: The Cabinet of Ministers of Uzbekistan issued Resolution No. 75, introducing new sustainability rating incentives for business entities collaborating with scientific researchers on green technologies.
paragraphs: On February 23, 2026, the Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Uzbekistan issued Resolution No. 75, titled 'On measures to develop cooperation between business entities and the scientific community.' This resolution establishes a direct national framework linking the business sector with university researchers, promoting the commercialization and integration of scientific developments into practical production.

Under this regulation, business entities that collaborate with scientific institutes (such as BSTU) to implement new environmental and technical developments into their production processes will be awarded 5 additional points in the official 'Entrepreneurs’ Sustainability Rating'. This rating, integrated with the Tax Committee's systems, directly influences credit facilities, tax preferences, and compliance procedures for businesses.

To facilitate this collaboration, the Innovation Development Agency under the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovations, in partnership with the Chamber of Commerce and Industry, will develop a Special Electronic Platform by July 1, 2026. This platform will contain a database of newly created scientific developments, a register of active researchers and their topics, and an AI-powered matchmaking tool to connect businesses with relevant scientists.

Furthermore, the resolution specifies that pilot and experimental work for scientists and business entities implementing these green developments will be financed directly by the Innovation Support Fund within the framework of annual competitions. Priority funding and selection will be granted in national science competitions to researchers who align their work with solving specific, documented problems submitted by industry partners.
articles.author: Ministry of Higher Education & Innovation

articles.title: International Conference: Eco-Digital Future
articles.excerpt: BSTU hosted the International Conference 'Eco-Digital Futures: Synergising Green Innovation, Sustainable Education, Economy and Tourism' bringing together researchers from across Central Asia and beyond.
paragraphs: Bukhara State Technical University proudly hosted the International Conference titled 'Eco-Digital Futures: Synergising Green Innovation, Sustainable Education, Economy and Tourism'. The conference brought together professors, researchers, students, and industry representatives from across Central Asia, Europe, and Asia to exchange knowledge on integrating ecological and digital solutions for a sustainable future.

The conference featured keynote sessions organized across seven specialized sections: Track I focused on Green & Digital Innovation for a Sustainable Future (renewable energy, smart grids, low-carbon technologies, and AI for environmental monitoring). Track II addressed Sustainable, Inclusive & Quality Education in the Digital Era (technical & vocational education, smart learning, and green campus approaches). Track III covered Green Economy & Digital Entrepreneurship (green business models, ESG strategies, and carbon trading). Track IV focused on Sustainable Tourism & Smart Destinations (eco-tourism, smart villages, and cultural heritage preservation).

Tracks V through VII examined Policy, Governance & Community Engagement (green technology policies, smart governance, and youth empowerment), Digital Futures for Health, Well-being & Climate Resilience (smart healthcare, disaster resilience, and climate-smart agriculture), and Cross-Border Collaboration & Global Partnerships. Accepted papers were compiled into the official Conference Proceedings, with outstanding papers nominated for Scopus-indexed and other major international databases.

The event culminated in a joint declaration signed by participating universities to promote collaborative research in sustainable technologies. Organizing Committee Chairman Komil Shokirov (+998936206169, komil.wp@gmail.com) thanked the international delegates for their contributions to shaping the eco-digital future.
articles.author: International Relations Office

articles.title: Eco-Plogging: A Step Towards Cleanliness and Healthy Lifestyle
articles.excerpt: In cooperation with tutor of the Faculty of Engineering Nodira Hakimova and first-year students, the 'Eco-plogging' event was organized to increase ecological culture, promote a healthy lifestyle, and keep the environment clean.
paragraphs: In cooperation with the tutor of the Faculty of Engineering, Nodira Hakimova, and first-year students, the 'Eco-plogging' event was organized with the aim of increasing ecological culture, promoting a healthy lifestyle, and keeping the environment clean.

Eco-plogging is an innovative environmental initiative that combines jogging with picking up litter — a concept that originated in Sweden and has now gained global recognition as an effective way to engage youth in environmental responsibility.

During the event, students cleaned the areas from waste, demonstrating a clear example of love for nature and a responsible attitude toward the environment. Through this event, young people increased their physical activity, strengthened their ecological awareness, and once again realized that protecting nature is the duty of every person.
The event was met with great enthusiasm from students and faculty alike, with plans to organize similar initiatives on a monthly basis throughout the academic year.
articles.author: Faculty of Engineering Eco-Committee

articles.title: Eco-Active Students Plogging Campaign: Protect Nature — Create the Future!
articles.excerpt: Under the slogan 'My Green University', eco-active students at Bukhara State Technical University organized a plogging campaign titled 'Protect Nature — Create the Future!' to maintain campus cleanliness.
paragraphs: At Bukhara State Technical University, eco-active students organized an impactful plogging campaign titled 'Protect Nature — Create the Future!' under the slogan 'My Green University.' The campaign brought together students from various departments to clean up the campus grounds while engaging in physical activity.

All students actively participated in the event, demonstrating their high ecological responsibility and civic engagement. Equipped with waste collection bags and gloves, the participants jogged across the university campus, collecting recyclable materials, plastic bottles, and paper waste.

This initiative aims not only to maintain cleanliness within the university grounds but also to encourage young people to take environmental issues seriously. By combining sport with community service, the event promoted a healthy lifestyle alongside environmental awareness.

Eco-active students at BSTU consistently engage in such green initiatives throughout the academic year. The university supports these student-led actions as part of its broader commitment to fostering a sustainable, eco-friendly campus environment.
articles.author: BSTU Youth Union Eco-Committee

articles.title: Inter-Neighborhood Eco-Plogging: Youth Uniting for a Cleaner Environment
articles.excerpt: An inter-neighborhood eco-plogging event organized by the Youth Union of BSTU brought students together to clean the territory of the Pridastgir neighborhood, demonstrating the power of collective environmental action.
paragraphs: An inter-neighborhood eco-plogging event was organized by the coordinators of the Youth Union of Bukhara State Technical University. Within the framework of this initiative, student youth united and carried out environmental cleanup activities in the territory of the Pridastgir neighborhood.

During the event, accumulated waste in streets and public places was cleared, contributing to making the area cleaner and more orderly. Student volunteers worked systematically across the neighborhood, covering parks, roadways, and public gathering areas.

Eco-plogging not only served to protect nature, but also contributed to raising environmental awareness among youth, promoting a healthy lifestyle, and strengthening teamwork. The collaborative spirit of the event demonstrated the power of organized student action in contributing to community welfare.

The Youth Union of BSTU plans to expand this initiative to all neighborhoods adjacent to the university campus, aiming to make a visible and lasting positive impact on the urban environment of Bukhara city.
articles.author: Youth Union of BSTU

articles.title: The Prosperity of the Homeland Begins with the Mahalla – Nationwide Hashar
articles.excerpt: Professors, teachers, and students of BSTU participated in the nationwide charity hashar held under the national slogan 'The prosperity of the homeland begins, first of all, with the mahalla.'
paragraphs: Bukhara State Technical University professors, teachers, and students actively participated in the nationwide charity hashar held under the national slogan 'The prosperity of the homeland begins, first of all, with the mahalla.' This annual national initiative mobilizes citizens across Uzbekistan to clean and beautify their communities.

The BSTU contingent participated in community beautification activities across several mahallas of Bukhara, planting trees, cleaning public areas, and participating in the renovation of community parks and green spaces. The university contributed both labor and planting materials for the initiative.

Hashar is a traditional Uzbek community practice of collective voluntary labor for the common good. BSTU's active participation reflects the university's commitment to embodying sustainable values not just within its campus, but also in the wider community it serves.

The nationwide hashar, organized under government directives, aims to create a sense of collective responsibility for the environment and community spaces. BSTU is committed to making annual hashar participation a cornerstone of its civic and environmental engagement programs.
articles.author: Community Engagement Committee

articles.title: BSTU Joins President's 'Green Space' National Tree-Planting Campaign
articles.excerpt: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev participated in tree-planting within the 'Green Space' national project and launched the National Dendrology Garden. Professors, teachers, and students of BSTU also actively participated.
paragraphs: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev participated in the tree-planting event within the framework of the 'Green Space' national project and officially launched the establishment of the National Dendrology Garden. Professors, teachers, and students of Bukhara State Technical University actively participated in the tree-planting event held under this prestigious national project.

BSTU's participation in the Green Space campaign reflects the university's deep alignment with the national agenda for environmental development. The university mobilized hundreds of participants — faculty members, students, and administrative staff — to participate in planting saplings across designated areas of Bukhara.

The trees planted through this initiative are selected for their suitability to the semi-arid climate of the Bukhara region, ensuring high survival rates and long-term environmental benefit. These include drought-resistant native species such as saxaul, elm, and poplar varieties.

The Green Space national project aims to plant tens of millions of trees across Uzbekistan, significantly increasing the country's green coverage and combating desertification. BSTU's active contribution to this initiative demonstrates the university's commitment to national environmental goals.
articles.author: Environmental Science Department

articles.title: BSTU Students Plant Trees in Karakalpakstan Under 'Eco-Culture' Project
articles.excerpt: Within the framework of the nationwide 'Eco-Culture' project, students of Bukhara State Technical University actively participated in a tree-planting campaign organized in the Republic of Karakalpakstan.
paragraphs: Within the framework of the nationwide 'Eco-Culture' project, students of Bukhara State Technical University actively participated in a tree-planting campaign organized in the Republic of Karakalpakstan. The initiative brought together university students from across Uzbekistan to contribute to the greening of this region.

The saplings planted by the students serve as an important initiative aimed at greening the area, improving the ecological environment, and protecting nature. The Karakalpakstan region faces particularly acute environmental challenges due to desertification near the former Aral Sea, making tree-planting initiatives there critically important.

BSTU students participated alongside peers from other universities, planting drought-resistant tree species across designated areas identified by regional environmental authorities. The campaign was organized as part of the broader national effort to restore ecological balance in areas affected by the Aral Sea disaster.

This experience gave BSTU students a first-hand understanding of environmental restoration challenges and practical conservation skills. The university plans to expand student participation in inter-regional environmental campaigns as part of its commitment to producing environmentally conscious graduates.
articles.author: BSTU Student Volunteer Corps

articles.title: Eco-Active Students: Building a Green Generation at BSTU
articles.excerpt: BSTU's Eco-Active Students program engages hundreds of students in environmental awareness campaigns, workshops, and community cleanup activities throughout the academic year.
paragraphs: Bukhara State Technical University's Eco-Active Students (Ekofaol talabalar) program is one of the university's most impactful sustainability initiatives. The program engages hundreds of students across all faculties in environmental awareness campaigns, workshops, practical clean-up activities, and community greening projects.

The program was formally aligned with the national agenda under Clause 32 of the 'Roadmap' approved by Resolution No. PQ-184 of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan, dated May 15, 2025. This presidential resolution mandated each higher education institution in Uzbekistan to establish a separate, regularly updated 'Eco-Active Students' section on its portal, documenting students' environmental engagement.

Key activities under this program include landscaping drives, park maintenance, and tree-planting events aligned with the nationwide 'Yashil Makon' (Green Space) project. In compliance with the secretariat's directives, the university coordinates these initiatives and registers reports through the 'edo.ijro.uz' execution system to the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovations, contributing data for subsequent reports to the Cabinet of Ministers, Accounts Chamber, and Ministry of Justice.

Eco-Active Students at BSTU are recognized as leaders in the national student environmental movement, with multiple award-winning projects presented at national and regional environmental conferences. The program exemplifies BSTU's commitment to producing graduates who are not only technically proficient, but also responsible stewards of the environment.
articles.author: BSTU Youth Union Eco-Committee
